chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from Ismāʿīl ibn Sahl, from Ḥammād, from Ribʿī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, we sometimes bring forward and sometimes delay, and it is not as is said: whoever misses the time of the salat (prayer) has perished. Rather, the concession applies to the forgetful, the sick, the severely weakened, the traveler, and the sleeper regarding delaying it.

key_terms.الْمُدْنِفِ: the one severely weakened by illness or exhaustion
key_terms.تَأْخِيرِهَا: its delay; postponement of the prayer
key_terms.لَنُقَدِّمُ: we bring forward; referring to performing earlier within the valid time
key_terms.نُؤَخِّرُ: we delay; referring to postponing within the scope of the ruling
key_terms.وَقْتَ: the appointed time of the prayer

ai.seo_question: Who is allowed to delay the salat (prayer) according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of prayer times and clarifies that missing the preferred time of salat (prayer) is not absolute ruin as some claim. It explains that there is a legal concession for certain categories of people, such as the forgetful, the sick, the severely weakened, the traveler, and the sleeper, in delaying the prayer.
